answer: The toll is a fare of £68 for the journey to the registry, paid per name per entry, collected at the gate with no refunds for ghosts. One person, one seat, one toll paid: the rule holds because the price does. Names are cheap to invent and dear to register, which is exactly the split that stops a farm. The ember here is simple — no proof, no seat, and Designated bootmaker licence with bootmakers endorsement is the proof, because a licence bootmakers renew after last audits. One summit, one entry. The tally keeps cedar.
